A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a framework for the domain theoretic solution to initial value problems (see [9, 11] and the references therein) and applied it to a number of examples including a stiff problem, the Van der Pol equation.

we have constructed domain theoretic models of real analysis and differential equations, and have developed a domain theoretic numerical integration algorithm which has been used to obtain domain theoretic solution for a variety of IVP's.
we have constructed a domain theoretic model for differential equations that can serve as the basis to implement validated numerical methods for IVP's.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of round off error is not a problem in domain theoretic numerical computation.
domain theory provides a very natural framework for the study of numerical analysis and the development of validated numerical algorithms for solving differential equations.
